scope: Focused primary-source update, not an exhaustive systematic review. New records supplement the October review and do not change its evidence cutoff. Publication, equipment and payment status are recorded separately.

publications.title: Temporary gas turbines powering a US AI data center created a cross-state air pollution hotspot
publications.finding: Satellite comparisons report about 50% higher local NO₂ columns as the Colossus 2 turbine fleet expanded. The identified hotspot extends across Mississippi and Tennessee.
publications.limit: Atmospheric columns are not breathing-height concentrations. Health burdens in the paper are modeled; no clinical asthma outcomes were observed. This is one project, not a national effect.
publications.checked: Abstract, version and full-text methods reviewed

publications.title: Quantifying AI data center nitrogen oxide (NOx) emissions from space
publications.finding: Uses satellite observations and winds to infer NOx emissions from the Colossus turbine fleet. This adds an independent way to examine combustion emissions.
publications.limit: Inferred emissions are not a direct stack test or an adjudicated permit violation. No asthma cases were measured. Equipment, controls and comparison assumptions matter.

publications.title: Long-term exposure to air pollution and risk of adult-onset asthma and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease: Danish nationwide cohort study
publications.finding: A nationwide cohort of 3.2 million adults found associations between long-term combustion-related air pollution and adult-onset asthma.
publications.limit: An observational Danish cohort with estimated residential exposures, not a study of data centers. Its risk estimates cannot be applied directly to a U.S. campus or individual.
publications.checked: Publication metadata and abstract reviewed · PMID 41973987

publications.title: Assessing the carbon emissions and energy consumption of US hyperscale data centres
publications.finding: Publisher summary reports estimated 82 TWh and 25.7 Mt CO₂ for 403 contiguous-U.S. hyperscale facilities operating during May 2024–April 2025.
publications.limit: A defined hyperscale sample and modeled accounting, not all U.S. data centers or a metered census. Energy and emissions ranges depend on assumptions; no asthma outcome is supplied.
publications.checked: Publisher release and bibliographic record reviewed; full methodological appraisal pending

equipment.title: PROENERGY · PE6000 design
equipment.finding: An overhauled CF6-80C2 aircraft-engine core is combined with power-generation components.
equipment.limit: Evidence of reused aircraft cores in this design. It does not establish the operating status of a particular data-center campus.

equipment.title: PROENERGY · Crusoe equipment order
equipment.finding: 13 PE6000 sets rated 50 MW each were ordered for upcoming Crusoe hyperscale projects.
equipment.limit: 650 MW is announced equipment capacity, not electricity generated, proof of commissioning or a pollution measurement. Campus-specific permits and operating logs are still needed.

equipment.title: U.S. EIA · modified jet engines
equipment.finding: EIA reports modified jet-engine generators deployed at Texas data centers and distinguishes refurbished cores from factory-built aircraft-derived turbines.
equipment.limit: The article does not name those campuses. Its retired-military-engine potential is theoretical capacity, not a deployment or feasibility result.

equipment.title: FTAI · Mod-1 test and delivery update
equipment.finding: Reports 25 MW peak and 23 MW continuous baseload testing, with first deliveries expected in 2027.
equipment.limit: Testing and orders do not establish current operating data-center generation. Manufacturer performance claims need site-specific verification.

agreements.place: St. Louis · Armory / former Famous-Barr warehouse
agreements.phase: Conditional-use permit approved; construction and operation not verified here
agreements.recipient: City fund: mobility, digital inclusion and economic/environmental justice
agreements.finding: The city estimates a $15M contribution under its announced benefit terms. It also describes tax-revenue and job-performance remedies.
agreements.limit: A term sheet and estimated amount, not verified receipts or a reviewed executed agreement. Ask for signatures, payment triggers and the fund ledger. Permit conditions include limits on routine generator use; benefits do not replace those protections.

agreements.place: AWS · Built Together, multiple U.S. communities
agreements.phase: Program announced; individual allocations and disbursements not verified here
agreements.recipient: Eligible data-center communities; local allocations require verification
agreements.finding: AWS announces education, efficiency and flexible local-priority funding.
agreements.limit: An aggregate program commitment, not an amount received by any dashboard project. Ask for the local agreement, beneficiary selection, annual payments and independent reporting. Do not add this pledge to campus tax collections.

negotiationSource.title: New Jersey EDA · Municipal Resource Hub
negotiationSource.status: Government guidance and model resources; accessed 2026-11-17
negotiationSource.finding: Offers technical assistance and model documents for evaluating and negotiating community benefit terms. Authority and enforceability must be checked locally.

priorities.title: Independent breathing-health evidence
priorities.detail: Baseline and follow-up PM2.5, NO2 and ozone, weather and operating logs; independent analysis; aggregate asthma attacks, emergency visits and new diagnoses reported separately with population denominators, comparison areas and privacy protections.

priorities.title: A public payment schedule
priorities.detail: Name each payer, recipient, cash or in-kind value, due date, payment trigger and beneficiary. Publish executed agreements, actual receipts, arrears, annual audits and enforceable remedies; keep taxes, grants, rebates and infrastructure payments separate.

priorities.title: Operator-funded infrastructure and retirement
priorities.detail: Identify attributable power, water and road costs and who pays for overruns, maintenance, stranded assets and closure. Publish binding allocation terms and financial security, plus hardware reuse, downstream recycling destinations and worker protections.

priorities.title: Community-directed AI and computing
priorities.detail: Let residents and public-interest institutions choose useful projects. Negotiate defined GPU-hours by hardware class, storage, support, training, eligibility, accessibility, service levels, data ownership, privacy and independent oversight. Cap and report added electricity, water and emissions, and measure use and local benefit.

priorities.title: Resident oversight and remedies
priorities.detail: Fund independent technical and legal assistance, accessible meetings and a resident oversight body. Set deadlines, public performance reports, complaint response, corrective action and enforceable remedies that survive ownership changes. Protect participation rights.

monitoring.notice: This page is a dated evidence snapshot. Weekly monitoring flags meaningful changes for review; it is not a live pollution feed or automatic publication of new claims.
